name: Phone History
subtitle: An on-device activity journal
description:
Phone History keeps a private, on-device journal of text context as you move between apps.

Temporary screen frames are processed into bounded text observations and discarded. When the Apple system model is available, observations become short activity memories with supporting evidence. History is sampled and partial: brief or protected screens may be missed, and summaries are inferences rather than proof of taps or actions.

Choose a storage budget, pause capture in the app or Control Center, and inspect or export your history. A desktop you explicitly approve can read memories and evidence over the same Wi-Fi. Current screenshots need separate permission. No cloud relay or analytics service is included.

This version requires Developer Mode and one-time developer pairing through your own trusted Mac. After setup, capture runs on the iPhone using an embedded local VPN worker. iOS displays its VPN status, and capture cannot run alongside another packet-tunnel VPN. No separate VPN app is required.

Phone History is open source. Read the setup and coverage limitations before installing.
review_notes:
Capture uses an embedded NEPacketTunnelProvider with a narrow local route to the phone's developer services. It performs authenticated remote developer pairing, reads AX audit text/metadata and temporary DVT screenshot frames, runs Vision OCR on-device, and discards pixels. No focus movement, inspector highlighting, touch injection or keystroke interception is used.

Developer Mode and a one-time remote pairing record from the recipient's own trusted Mac are required. Records and private keys are never bundled, shared with Apple or exported to desktop agents. The setup and conversion helper are documented at https://github.com/Panchangam18/phone-history. Without that recipient-specific setup, live capture cannot start.

Desktop access is optional and requires on-phone fingerprint approval; screenshots require a separate permission. The standard iOS VPN indicator is visible. Saved data is protected by native iOS file protection; desktop identity keys use Keychain and CryptoKit authenticated encryption. The developer transport additionally uses third-party cryptographic implementations. Export-compliance classification remains to be determined by the account holder.

The app has no account login, subscriptions, advertising, analytics or cloud relay. Its developer-service dependency, background tunnel use and activity-recording indication require explicit eligibility review; they are not presented as approved public capture APIs.

The journal records bounded context already visible to the device owner for private recollection. Capture and summarization stay on the phone; temporary pixels are discarded. We receive no captured content. There is no third-party content catalog, social-account login, audio/video downloader or background upload to us. Optional export goes only to the user-approved desktop. Build 65 excludes the history/trust folder and diagnostic mirror from system backups; older backup copies are not removed.

Build 69's on-device summary LLM writes activity titles and prose directly from timestamped evidence. Its prompt controls wording, specifics, chronology and uncertainty; code checks size limits and supporting quote occurrence without sentence templates or semantic classifiers. Model interpretation can be wrong. If generation fails, evidence is preserved and summarization is deferred. The journal remains partial and is not a verified tap or action log.
